requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m appworker succeeded; id shows uid=1001(appworker) both before and after restart, confirming the account exists and persists.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256; effective values verified live via a 'su - appworker' login shell (pam_limits applied) showing ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart, boot identity change, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot id (e9250ad1...) and healthy account/limits state captured, reboot issued and acknowledged, node became unreachable then reachable again with a different boot id (88f7d64a...), and account, config file, and effective login-shell ulimits were re-verified intact post-restart. The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the boot-identity change (before_prepare vs after_executor).

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and configured PAM limits (nofile 8192, nproc 256) exactly as required, verifying the effective limits via an actual login shell both before and after a full node restart. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: pre-restart boot id and healthy state, restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot id, and full re-verification of account/config/effective-limits state, all cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is high, with only a trivial reboot-log artifact as incidental residue.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so no independent package-state consistency check exists for node1.
Effective ulimit verification relied on 'su - appworker' rather than a full interactive login session (e.g., via getty/sshd), though pam_limits is applied identically in both paths for RHEL7.

operational_hygiene.summary: All six executor commands map directly to task fulfillment (user/limits creation and verification) or the required restart-evidence protocol (baseline capture, reboot, reconnection, post-restart re-verification); none are unrelated troubleshooting experiments. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a byproduct of the nohup-backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' redirect used to safely disconnect before the node went down — a low-risk, single small log file with no security or functional impact, not a broad or destructive mutation. Listening-socket and other /tmp diffs between before/after snapshots are simply the same services restarting with new PIDs/boot-id-derived paths after the required reboot, not executor-introduced drift.
